title: Quick look 2: Lane B on public Terminal-Bench 2.0 tasks
author: GSTA-12
question: On real coding tasks graded by whether the result works, does gstack beat no skills and a length-matched placebo, on Opus 5.5 and two cheap models, and how much of the gap to Opus does gstack close?

arms.name: gstack
arms.description: gstack installed for Claude Code by its own setup.

arms.name: placebo
arms.description: gstack's names and routing text, each SKILL.md body replaced by non-procedural prose within 5% of its tokens.

models.route: openrouter Anthropic Messages, provider only [deepseek], no fallbacks

tasks.source: terminal-bench@2.0 at 69671fbaac6d, 20 tasks chosen by a fixed rule over published per-trial results (tasks/selection.md)
tasks.replacement: Before the first paid call, a task whose oracle fails is replaced by the next reserve; after it, an ungradable task is dropped and reported.

secondary.definition: Metered cost of graded trials over passes
A Skill call or a SKILL.md read

rules: Share of the Opus gap closed per cheap model, over tasks graded in all three cells, with the share of resamples where the gap is positive.
Tier A (ranks 1 to 10) is a secondary set.

approval.source: gate 1 of the v1 plan (first cap $500), moved up on "It should be fast like this week"

money.reservation: The proxy reserves each session's cap before it starts and refuses any request whose worst case would pass it.
money.stop_rule: When the ledger refuses a reserve, no new session starts and the run is reported incomplete; never retried to change a result.
order: Replicates 2 and 3 on Haiku and DeepSeek
Replicate 2 on Opus, then more while money remains

peg.note: The Data API needs an OpenRouter key; the route check reads it once the key lands and records meta.as_of with the results.

limits: 20 tasks at 1 to 3 trials per cell: exploratory estimates.
DeepSeek is metered at the peak price, so its costs are upper bounds.
deviations: Verifier timeouts doubled for every task, as Terminal-Bench 2.1 later did.
